(`governance.md`'s no-raw-payload-logging principle, applied to user-uploaded content
rather than model/source output). `extracted_text` is the `markitdown`-converted Markdown
for a document attachment (`.docx`/`.xlsx`/`.pptx`/`.pdf`/...); it is `None` for an image

post.description:

cookies, and return the provider authorize URL for the client to navigate to.

get.description:
OAuth redirect target: verify `state`, exchange the code, verify the ID token, resolve the
identity (login/signup or link), issue the session cookies, then hand the browser back to the
frontend. The provider lands the browser here as a full top-level navigation (per
`google_redirect_uri`/`line_redirect_uri` in settings pointing directly at this route) — so
every outcome, success or failure, must end in a redirect, never a bare JSON body the user
would otherwise be staring at.

Begin linking a provider to the already-signed-in user — same as begin, but the callback
will attach the verified identity to the current account instead of logging in fresh.

get.description:
Second half of a link started from another origin: redeem the ticket, set the flow cookies
on *this* origin (the one the provider will redirect back to), and send the browser on to the
provider. A forged or expired ticket goes to the error screen.

post.description:
Rotate the refresh token and mint a fresh access token. A reused (rotated-out) token is a
theft signal — the whole session family is revoked and the caller must sign in again.

post.description:
Move the caller's live subscription to another tier / interval / BYOK variant. Paddle's
customer portal only offers card updates and cancellation, so plan changes are made here
against Paddle's subscription API (prorated immediately by Paddle). The local row and tier are
refreshed from Paddle straight away; the webhook that follows is then a no-op.

Create a Paddle checkout transaction for the selected plan, tagged with the user id so the
webhook can attribute the resulting subscription back to this account. A user who already has a
live subscription changes or cancels it in the Paddle portal instead - a second checkout would
bill them twice.

never guessed, when Paddle can't be asked.

A link into Paddle's customer portal. `overview` is the portal home (plan, payments,

handling, cancellation and invoices are all Paddle's. Falls back to the subscription's own
management links if a portal session can't be created.
Undo a scheduled cancellation, or restart a paused subscription.

get.description:
The caller's current subscription, reconciled against the live Paddle API so a dropped or

post.description:
Recover a checkout whose webhook never arrived: look the transaction up at Paddle and adopt

raw body first, then applies the idempotent, order-safe entitlement mapping.

console). The `X-Line-Signature` header is base64(HMAC-SHA256(channel secret, raw body)); a
request without a valid one is refused before the body is read as JSON. Handled events: a
message carrying a link code binds the sender; `follow` sends instructions; `unfollow` drops
the link (the user blocked the account, so pushes would fail).

get.description:
Live-ish quote feed (SSE) via the shared demand-driven poller.

One poller per worker fetches each demanded symbol once per tick — through `dispatch_tool`
over `get_price_quote`, exactly the one-shot `/quote` path — and fans the snapshot out to
every subscriber, so N clients watching one symbol cost one upstream fetch, not N. Subscribing
increments a Redis demand refcount; disconnecting decrements it, and at zero the symbol leaves
the demand set so the poller stops touching it (bounded observation, never an unattended
scan). Each `quote` frame carries `as_of` (the snapshot's own source timestamp) and
`market_open`; off-hours the poller idles.

Entitlement is unchanged from the one-shot read: the shared fetch pulls real data, and each
connection re-applies `get_price_quote`'s own masking to its frames (via the same
`MaskedTeaser` shape `dispatch_tool` uses), so an unentitled caller sees the masked teaser per
tick, never a hard error. Over-cap symbols (per-connection or global) are dropped from this
subscription rather than crashing the connection.

Queue a steering message into the running turn (redirect, no cancel).

The steering text is recorded on the live turn handle (`RunningTurn.steering`) and a
`steering.accepted` frame is published to the turn's stream so the client reflects it. The
running `AgentLoop` (for the `single`-framework interactive root lane — see
`Orchestrator.run`'s `steering_source` docstring for the fan-out-lane scope note) polls that
same handle at its next Step boundary (`agent.loop.AgentLoop._inject_steering`), folds the
message in as a new user-role turn, and clears it — never redirecting mid-Step, only between
Steps, so an in-flight tool dispatch always finishes first.

get.description:
Attach to a thread's running turn and stream its remaining frames, with durable
`Last-Event-ID` resume when the transport backend supports it.

Two paths, chosen by the configured transport:

- **Same worker (or single-process `memory` backend):** if this worker holds the live turn in
  its registry, attach to the in-process bus directly. Live-only — the in-memory backend has
  no durable/cross-worker log to replay from.
- **Cross worker (`redis` backend):** subscribe to the turn's live Redis channel first, then
  replay everything the client missed from the durable log, then emit live frames — filtering
  out any whose `seq` the replay already covered. A reconnect after the turn ended still
  replays the tail from the durable log.

A reconnect with nothing to attach to and no durable reader returns an immediately-closing
stream rather than an error.

post.description:
Edit a user message + resend — creates a NEW branch: a new user turn as a sibling of the
original (same parent message), with a new assistant turn as its child. The original user
turn's row is never touched — canonical immutability (governance) means an edit must never
rewrite an existing message row, only add a new sibling subtree.

Reuses the same tree-branching shape as `regenerate`: the new user turn's `parent_message_id`
is the ORIGINAL user turn's own parent (so it lands as a sibling, exactly what `switch_branch`
would navigate between afterward), and the new assistant turn is then appended as that new
user turn's child. Runs through the same `api.turn_driver.start_turn_stream` seam as
`/agent/query` and `regenerate` — same guardrail/entitlement/journal path.

Automatic branch-summary generation for the branch being left is not performed here, for the
same reason `switch_branch` doesn't do it either: that needs a cheap-role `LLMClient` handle
the interface layer does not hold today (see `switch_branch`'s own docstring). The branch
itself is real and immediately navigable via `switch_branch`; the summary is a follow-up.

Record 👍/👎 + an optional short comment on a turn — a real, persisted write.

Deliberately minimal: this is a rating capture, not the quality-score/alert pipeline the
stale spec once described (rolling 7-day score, alert thresholds, admin `quality`/`alerts`/
`recent` endpoints) — that remains unbuilt and is a dedicated follow-up. `submit` upserts on
`(turn_id, user_id)`, so a re-submit (thumbs-down then thumbs-up) updates the one row rather
than accumulating duplicates.

Re-run the same user input that produced `turn_id`'s assistant answer, producing a NEW
sibling assistant turn — a version, not an edit of history.

Reuses the exact tree-branching primitive `switch_branch` relies on: `ConversationStore.
append_turn`'s `parent_message_id` is what makes a new turn a *sibling* rather than a
descendant — passing the source user turn's own last message id (the same parent the
original assistant turn was appended under) makes the new assistant turn a sibling of the one
being regenerated, both hanging off the same user message. No new store method was needed;
`append_turn` already supports this shape. The turn-driver invocation is the same
`api.turn_driver.start_turn_stream` seam `/agent/query` uses — same guardrail/entitlement/
journal path, no bypass — seeded with the original turn's user text instead of a fresh
message. `regenerate_of` on the new turn records which turn it re-ran.

The ingest leader publishes a lightweight `{capability, market, as_of, scope}` signal the

and relays each frame so the frontend invalidates exactly the affected keys instead of waiting
out a fixed time boundary.

post.description:
Resend reports what happened to each email. Three outcomes matter here: a hard bounce
(`email.bounced`, type Permanent), a spam complaint (`email.complained`) and Resend's own
`email.suppressed`. The address is recorded and never emailed again. A soft bounce, delivery
and open events are acknowledged and ignored. The request must carry a valid Svix signature;
with no secret configured every request is refused.
